q: What is the Grading Coach?
a: The Grading Coach has guided lessons, one-time context hints and Ask the coach. A lesson walks you through one task, one step at a time, on your own clip: each step says what to do and why, outlines the control, and waits until you've actually done it before moving on.

q: How do I start a lesson?
a: Click Lessons (Resolve workflow: the page bar at the bottom, left of Home; Premiere workflow: the header's right side), or Help ▸ Grading Lessons…. Click Start (Again for a finished one) beside a lesson; the coach card appears at the bottom right. Scripts: `coach.showLessons` opens the list, `coach.lessons` lists them, `coach.start` with `{"lesson": "first-grade"}` starts one and `coach.state` reports the step.

q: What do Back, Skip and Exit do on the lesson card?
a: The card shows the title, Step n of m, the provenance, what to do and Why. Back (`coach.back`) goes to the previous step, Skip (`coach.skip`) moves on without doing it, Exit (`coach.exit`) stops the lesson. Next only appears on reading or looking steps; every other step finishes when you do it. At the end: Lesson complete, and Close removes the card.

q: What is the coloured outline during a lesson?
a: It marks the control the step is about: a button, slider, wheel or panel, scrolled into view once if it's in a list. If it isn't visible at all the card says the highlighted control isn't on screen yet; follow the step text to reveal it.

q: Where are finished lessons stored?
a: In your preferences (`color.coach.completed`); `coach.lessons` shows `completed: true`. Seen hints are remembered the same way (`color.coach.hintsSeen`).

q: Which commands manage hints for an agent?
a: `coach.hint` returns the hint on screen, whether hints are enabled and the ids already seen (`{"all": true}` adds every hint); `coach.dismissHint` closes it (`{"off": true}` also turns hints off); `coach.resetHints` forgets the hints shown so each can appear again.

q: What does From the guide mean under an answer?
a: Click Ask the coach (page bar, left of Home; Premiere: header top right), type your question in your own words and press Enter or Ask. Read the steps; click a step that names a control to outline it (click again to remove). With no steps, the lesson link starts the closest lesson. Under the answer, From the guide names the section the steps came from and its provenance, so you know whether a Resolve or Premiere habit applies.

q: What happens if I ask about a word the guide never uses?
a: For an "is there …" or "where is …" question about a word the guide never uses, the coach names that word: the guide doesn't mention it. If most of your words aren't in the guide, it says the guide doesn't cover this yet. It never invents an answer.

q: How is a hint triggered?
a: Each `[[hint]]` in `assets/coach/hints.toml` has a `when` list of triggers: a command with an optional `params` pattern, a control shown on screen (`element`), or a rule the engine checks on the grade (`rule = "qualifierAfterHeavyLook"`).

q: What can a lesson step expect?
a: A step's `expect` is one of: `{ command = "id" }` (or up to 8 ids) with optional `params` patterns (`gt`, `ge`, `lt`, `le`, `ne`, `any`, `nonzero`, `in`, lists item by item); `{ element = "automation.id" }` for open-this-tab steps; or `{ manual = true }` for Next. `already = "clipSelected"` finishes a step when any clip is selected. Limits: 64 KiB per file, 40 steps, 1 200 characters per text, patterns 6 deep and 64 values; unknown fields are refused.

q: What are the limits of a lesson file?
a: A step's `expect` is one of: `{ command = "id" }` (or up to 8 ids) with optional `params` patterns (`gt`, `ge`, `lt`, `le`, `ne`, `any`, `nonzero`, `in`, lists item by item); `{ element = "automation.id" }` for open-this-tab steps; or `{ manual = true }` for Next. `already = "clipSelected"` finishes a step when any clip is selected. Limits: 64 KiB per file, 40 steps, 1 200 characters per text, patterns 6 deep and 64 values; unknown fields are refused.

q: How is the assistant different from the keyword coach?
a: The keyword coach repeats the guide's own steps; the assistant, a small language model on your computer (SmolLM3 3B, 4-bit, about 2 GB), answers from the sections that fit. With a separate graphics card it takes about 2–4 s per answer (first words after about a second); on the processor 20–40 s. It is off until you tick Also ask the assistant, and the guide's answer is always shown above it.

q: What does General advice mean in an assistant answer?
a: Lines marked General advice are shown dimmer: they aren't from the guide. Sources lists the guide sections the answer used (or was given). Lines naming a button, command or shortcut the sections don't have are left out, and the box says how many.

q: How does an agent call the assistant?
a: `coach.assist {question}` returns an `id`; `coach.assistResult {id}` gives `pending` with `partial` text, or `done`; `coach.assistForget {id}` stops it. `style: "free"` lets the model write its own answer (it invented far more in tests), so `pick` is the default.

q: How do I open the Assistant chat?
a: Click Assistant in the page bar at the bottom, left of Home (Premiere workflow: the header top right). It opens floating, left of where the coach's cards appear. Type in the box at the bottom and press Enter or Send (Shift+Enter for a new line); Stop ends an answer early, New chat starts a new topic, and clicking Assistant again closes it.

q: Ask box or Assistant panel: which should I use?
a: Options: the Ask box is quicker for a single question and shows the guide's steps at once; the panel suits a conversation or keeping answers next to the controls they name. A beginner may find the floating panel easiest; docking it beside the panels you use most keeps it out of the picture's way.

q: What happens if the GPU fails during an answer?
a: Answers that start within about a second and finish in a few seconds mean the graphics card. Revolution's log file (Logs folder in its data folder) says LLM on the GPU with the card's name, or LLM: on the CPU with the reason. If the card fails mid-answer, Revolution carries on with the processor. Testers: `FILMCRAFT_LLM_GPU=0` forces the processor.
